Description: Farcaş, aged twenty-two, is an intrepid young Romanian Kenez governing the rugged highland forests and mountain valleys of North Oltenia. Specifically designated in the historic 1247 Joannite Diploma as the sovereign kenez of his ancestral territory, he commands immense authority. Athletic, sharp-witted, and naturally combative, he was raised on mountain horseback, renowned among his Vlach huntsmen as a vigilant warrior akin to a mountain wolf. Allied closely with his southern neighbor Voivode Litovoi, Farcaş forms the iron vanguard defying Hungarian territorial encroachments from Severin. A master of defensive geography, he expertly sets rockslides, deadfalls, and concealed palisades along mountain defiles, having mauled overconfident Western knights. Across his rugged domains, he fosters transhumant sheep herding and timber trade, maintaining a proud warrior militia ready to assemble at the horn's call. Farcaş lives by the ancestral code of Carpathian mountain freedom, determined that no foreign usurper shall breach the pristine wilderness of North Oltenia. Moving with astonishing agility through Carpathian ravines, he leads mountain hunters in setting camouflaged deadfalls, guaranteeing that invading detachments are decisively annihilated in the rocky wilderness without hope of escape. Their unwavering dedication and strategic foresight remain indispensable to the enduring independence and glory of the realm.
Motivations: Defend the vital strategic interests, honor, and enduring inheritance of the Bulgarian and Danubian domains.
Ensure maximum tactical efficiency, troop discipline, and logistical preparedness for impending frontier conflicts.
Uphold the Orthodox faith and Slavic heritage against foreign crusader incursions and nomad extortion alike.
Values: Unwavering fidelity to Orthodox Christian traditions and regional Slavic sovereignty.
Dedication to noble honor, military discipline, and the defense of Christian subjects from devastation.
Pragmatic statecraft grounded in historical precedent, strategic caution, and administrative order.
Fears: The loss of ancestral patrimony and regional prestige to foreign invaders or internal factional schism.
Catastrophic military defeat leaving the frontiers vulnerable to pillage by Latin or nomadic armies.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with crisp mountain fervor, youthful audacity, and uncompromising candor, delivering energetic commands that electrify his woodsmen.
